claim: The twin-arginine protein translocation system (Tat) transports folded proteins across the bacterial cytoplasmic membrane and the thylakoid membranes of plant chloroplasts.
source: The twin-arginine protein translocation system (Tat) transports folded proteins across the bacterial cytoplasmic membrane and the thylakoid membranes of plant chloroplasts.
evidence: This is a well-established fact about the Tat system supported by extensive prior research and represents established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: The Tat transporter is assembled from multiple copies of the membrane proteins TatA, TatB, and TatC.
source: The Tat transporter is assembled from multiple copies of the membrane proteins TatA, TatB, and TatC.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the composition of the Tat transporter.

claim: In the TatBC receptor complex the transmembrane helix of each TatB molecule is sandwiched between two TatC molecules.
source: In the TatBC receptor complex the transmembrane helix of each TatB molecule is sandwiched between two TatC molecules, with one of the inter-subunit interfaces incorporating a functionally important cluster of interacting polar residues.
evidence: This claim is supported by the co-evolution analysis, molecular modeling, and experimental validation presented in the manuscript.

claim: One of the inter-subunit interfaces in the TatBC complex incorporates a functionally important cluster of interacting polar residues.
source: In the TatBC receptor complex the transmembrane helix of each TatB molecule is sandwiched between two TatC molecules, with one of the inter-subunit interfaces incorporating a functionally important cluster of interacting polar residues.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that mutations in the polar cluster abolish Tat function.

claim: TatA associates with TatC at the polar cluster site.
source: Unexpectedly, we find that TatA also associates with TatC at the polar cluster site.
evidence: This is supported by co-evolution analysis and experimental data showing increased TatA binding when TatB is removed.

claim: Substrate binding triggers replacement of TatB by TatA at the polar cluster site.
source: Our data provide a structural model for assembly of the active Tat translocase in which substrate binding triggers replacement of TatB by TatA at the polar cluster site.
evidence: This is a mechanistic model inferred from the experimental observations and structural data.

claim: Protein transport by the Sec apparatus involves a threading mechanism and requires the substrate protein to be maintained in an unstructured state.
source: Protein transport by the Sec apparatus involves a threading mechanism and requires the substrate protein to be maintained in an unstructured state (Park and Rapoport, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The Tat system transports substrate proteins that have already achieved a folded conformation.
source: By contrast, the Tat (twin-arginine translocation) system transports substrate proteins that have already achieved a folded conformation (Berks, 2015; Cline, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Loss of the Tat pathway results in serious pleiotropic effects on major cellular processes including energy metabolism, nutrient acquisition, virulence, and formation of the cell envelope.
source: However, even under permissive growth conditions, loss of the Tat pathway results in serious pleiotropic effects on major cellular processes including energy metabolism, nutrient acquisition, virulence, and formation of the cell envelope (Berks et al., 2003; De Buck et al., 2008; Palmer and Berks, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The Tat transport system has been evolutionarily conserved in plant chloroplasts where it mediates protein import across the thylakoid membrane and is essential for the formation of a functional photosynthetic apparatus.
source: The Tat transport system has been evolutionarily conserved in plant chloroplasts where it mediates protein import across the thylakoid membrane and is essential for the formation of a functional photosynthetic apparatus (Celedon and Cline, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Minimal Tat systems found in some organisms contain a single type of TatA protein and one type of TatC molecule.
source: Minimal Tat systems found in some organisms contain a single type of TatA protein and one type of TatC molecule.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Tat system composition.

claim: Minimal Tat systems are assumed to be ancestral to the more common arrangement in which a second, functionally distinct member of the TatA family, called TatB, is also present.
source: These Tat systems are assumed to be ancestral to the more common arrangement in which a second, functionally distinct member of the TatA family, called TatB, is also present.
evidence: This is an inference based on phylogenetic considerations.

claim: E. coli has a third TatA family member called TatE which is functionally equivalent to TatA but is present at much lower concentration in the cell and not essential for Tat transport.
source: For example, E. coli has a third TatA family member called TatE which is functionally equivalent to TatA but is present at much lower concentration in the cell and not essential for Tat transport (Jack et al., 2001; Sargent et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Proteins are targeted to the Tat system by N-terminal signal peptides bearing the eponymous pair of arginine residues.
source: Proteins are targeted to the Tat system by N-terminal signal peptides bearing the eponymous pair of arginine residues (Berks, 1996; Chaddock et al., 1995; Stanley et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In E. coli and chloroplasts the signal peptide is recognized at the membrane by a receptor complex containing multiple copies of both TatB and TatC.
source: In E. coli and chloroplasts the signal peptide is recognized at the membrane by a receptor complex containing multiple copies of both TatB and TatC (Cline and Mori, 2001; Tarry et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Substrate binding to the TatBC complex leads to the recruitment and oligomerization of TatA protomers from a pool in the membrane to form the active translocation site.
source: Substrate binding to the TatBC complex leads to the recruitment and oligomerization of TatA protomers from a pool in the membrane to form the active translocation site (Alcock et al., 2013; Dabney-Smith et al., 2006; Rose et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Members of the TatA family conserve a core of two helical elements comprising a hydrophobic transmembrane helix (TMH) followed immediately by an amphipathic helix (APH).
source: Members of the TatA family conserve a core of two helical elements comprising a hydrophobic transmembrane helix (TMH) followed immediately by an amphipathic helix (APH).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about TatA family proteins.

claim: TatC is composed of six transmembrane helices (TM1-TM6) shaped like a cupped hand.
source: TatC is composed of six transmembrane helices (TM1-TM6) shaped like a cupped hand.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about TatC based on crystal structures.

claim: Ten out of the 12 most highly co-evolving sequence pairs are directed from one face of the TatA TMH toward surface-exposed residues in TM5 and TM6 of TatC.
source: Ten out of the 12 most highly co-evolving sequence pairs, including three with precision scores above 0.5, are directed from one face of the TatA TMH toward surface-exposed residues in TM5 and TM6 of TatC (Figure 1B,C and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by the co-evolution analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The evolutionarily coupled residues lie in the same order along the faces of the two proteins as expected of an authentic contact interface between TM helices.
source: The evolutionarily coupled residues lie in the same order along the faces of the two proteins as expected of an authentic contact interface between TM helices.
evidence: This is an inference from the co-evolution data that supports the validity of the predicted interface.

claim: The unusually short TatA TMH is well-matched in length to the section of the kinked TatC TM5 with which it primarily interacts.
source: It is also notable that the unusually short TatA TMH is well-matched in length to the section of the kinked TatC TM5 with which it primarily interacts.
evidence: This is an observation from structural analysis that supports the proposed interaction.

claim: The TatA and TatB proteins of plant chloroplasts have biochemical behavior that closely mirrors that of their E. coli counterparts.
source: The proposal that both TatA and TatB are able to use the same binding site on TatC is supported by the observation that the TatA and TatB proteins of plant chloroplasts have biochemical behavior that closely mirrors that of their E. coli counterparts (Cline, 2015), even though they are very similar in sequence to each other (Figure 2A, red star).
evidence: This is supported by citation and comparison to sequence data.

claim: Residue eight is most commonly a glutamic acid in all TatA family proteins.
source: Residue eight is most commonly a glutamic acid in all TatA family proteins.
evidence: This is supported by the sequence logo analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Glutamic acid at position eight is almost always present in TatB proteins.
source: Whilst this amino acid is almost always present in TatB proteins, TatA proteins often substitute the alternative polar amino acids histidine or glutamine, and TatAbasal proteins use glycine or serine at significant frequency.
evidence: This is supported by the sequence logo analysis.

claim: TatA proteins often substitute histidine or glutamine at position eight.
source: Whilst this amino acid is almost always present in TatB proteins, TatA proteins often substitute the alternative polar amino acids histidine or glutamine, and TatAbasal proteins use glycine or serine at significant frequency.
evidence: This is supported by the sequence logo analysis.

claim: The TatBC interface was simulated with E8 in either the protonated or deprotonated state.
source: The TatBC interface was simulated with E8 in either the protonated or deprotonated state.
evidence: This describes the computational methods used in the study.

claim: After minor equilibration of the interaction interface, the simulations settled to a stable state in which the two proteins remained tightly packed and where the secondary structure in the starting models was preserved.
source: After minor equilibration of the interaction interface, the simulations settled to a stable state in which the two proteins remained tightly packed and where the secondary structure in the starting models was preserved (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: The stability of the models provides computational support for the interaction site suggested by evolutionary methods.
source: The stability of the models provides computational support for the interaction site suggested by evolutionary methods.
evidence: This is an inference from the simulation results.

claim: The contact site on E. coli TatC could plausibly bind either TatA or TatB.
source: It also confirms that the contact site on E. coli TatC could plausibly bind either TatA or TatB.
evidence: This is an inference from the simulation results showing stability of both TatAC and TatBC complexes.

claim: The polar residue found at position eight in TatA and TatB participates in hydrogen-bonding interactions with some of its strongly co-evolving partner residues in TatC.
source: Detailed examination of the simulations shows that the polar residue found at position eight in TatA and TatB participates in hydrogen-bonding interactions with some of its strongly co-evolving partner residues in TatC (Figure 4C and Video 2).
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: In the case of TatB, the carboxylate side chain of deprotonated E8 acts as a hydrogen bond acceptor from both TatC T208 and Q215.
source: In the case of TatB, the carboxylate side chain of deprotonated E8 acts as a hydrogen bond acceptor from both TatC T208 and Q215.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: When TatB E8 is protonated, TatC T208 is the hydrogen bond acceptor from TatB E8.
source: These residue interactions are maintained when TatB E8 is protonated but now TatC T208 is the hydrogen bond acceptor from TatB E8.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: TatC Q215 acts as a hydrogen bond donor to TatA Q8.
source: TatC Q215 also acts as a hydrogen bond donor to TatA Q8.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: No hydrogen bonds are formed between TatA Q8 and TatC T208 in any of the simulations.
source: However, no hydrogen bonds are formed between TatA Q8 and TatC T208 in any of the simulations.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: Additional stabilization of the position of the TatA/TatB polar residue side chain arises from aliphatic interactions with the strongly co-evolving TatC residue M205.
source: Additional stabilization of the position of the TatA/TatB polar residue side chain arises from aliphatic interactions with the strongly co-evolving TatC residue M205.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: Other amino acid pairs commonly found at position eight in TatA family proteins and position 215 in TatC have the potential to hydrogen bond with each other.
source: Sequence analysis shows that other amino acid pairs commonly found at position eight in TatA family proteins and position 215 in TatC have the potential to hydrogen bond with each other (e.g. H8-Q215, K8-Q215, S8-H215).
evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis and structural inference.

claim: A polar interaction between the residues at positions eight and 215 is a general feature of the Tat system.
source: This suggests that a polar interaction between the residues at these positions is a general feature of the Tat system.
evidence: This is an inference from sequence and structural analysis.

claim: Polar contacts between membrane-spanning helices are rare, and normally of functional significance.
source: The prediction that TatA family proteins interact with TatC through an intramembrane cluster of polar amino acid residues is noteworthy because polar contacts between membrane-spanning helices are rare, and normally of functional significance (Popot and Engelman, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Plasmid p101C*TatBC directs expression of TatB and TatC at native levels and fully restores Tat transport activity to a ΔtatBC strain.
source: Plasmid p101C*TatBC directs expression of TatB and TatC at native levels and fully restores Tat transport activity to a ΔtatBC strain (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Neither the TatA Q8A nor TatB E8A variants supported detectable CueO export.
source: Neither the TatA Q8A nor TatB E8A variants supported detectable CueO export (Figure 5A; strains AQ8ABC and AE pBE8AC).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Cells of the TatB E8A variant were fully chained indicating a complete absence of Tat transport.
source: Cells of the TatB variant were also fully chained indicating a complete absence of Tat transport (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1; strain AE pBE8AC)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Cultures of the TatA Q8A variant contained both single cells and short chains suggesting retention of a very low level of Tat function.
source: whilst cultures of the TatA variant contained both single cells and short chains suggesting retention of a very low level of Tat function (Figure 5B; strain AQ8ABC).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The concentration of the TatB E8A variant in cell membranes is lower than that of the wild-type TatB protein.
source: Although the concentration of the TatB E8A variant in cell membranes is lower than that of the wild-type TatB protein (Figure 5C; strain AE pBE8AC), this cannot account for the complete loss of Tat function seen for the variant.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Removing the TMH polar residue of either TatA or TatB abolishes or severely compromises the transport of different Tat substrates.
source: Thus, removing the TMH polar residue of either TatA or TatB abolishes or severely compromises the transport of different Tat substrates.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on Q8A and E8A variants.

claim: The TatC MTQ variant (M205A/T208A/Q215A) was unable to support Tat transport.
source: We constructed a M205A/T208A/Q215A variant that contains substitutions of all three polar cluster residues in TatC and which is hereafter designated `MTQ'. This variant was unable to support Tat transport (Figure 5A,B; strain A pBCMTQ).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: All three single amino acid variants (M205A, T208A, Q215A) were able to suppress cell chaining and permit CueO export.
source: All three variants were able to suppress cell chaining and permit CueO export, although the amount of CueO reaching the periplasm was lower than that observed with the wild-type protein particularly in the T208A and Q215A variants (Figure 5A,B; strains A pBCM205A, A pBCT208A, and A pBCQ215A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: The combination of T208A with Q215A is sufficient to abolish CueO export and exhibits partial cell chaining.
source: Analysis of doubly substituted TatC variants showed that the combination of T208A with Q215A is sufficient to abolish CueO export and exhibits partial cell chaining (Figure 5A,B; strain A pBCT208A,Q215A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: It is the hydrogen bonding network in the polar cluster that is critical for transport.
source: This suggests that it is the hydrogen bonding network in the polar cluster that is critical for transport.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that double substitutions affecting hydrogen bonding abolish transport.

claim: TatA, TatB, and TatC were still present in the membranes of each TatC polar cluster variant studied.
source: Immunoblotting experiments confirm that TatA, TatB, and TatC were still present in the membranes of each TatC polar cluster variant studied (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Removal of either the TatA/TatB or TatC sides of the predicted polar cluster prevents Tat transport.
source: In summary, removal of either the TatA/TatB or TatC sides of the predicted polar cluster prevents Tat transport, consistent with the idea that the polar cluster plays a crucial role in the Tat system.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on polar cluster variants.

claim: The native E. coli TatBC complex binds TatA molecules even in the absence of substrate activation.
source: This confirms that the native E. coli TatBC complex binds TatA molecules even in the absence of substrate activation.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments with the FEA variant that blocks substrate binding.

claim: TatA has both constitutive and substrate-induced modes of interaction with the TatBC complex.
source: Thus, TatA has both constitutive and substrate-induced modes of interaction with the TatBC complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the co-immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: Constitutively associating TatA molecules represent only a small proportion of the total TatA present in the cell.
source: The constitutively associating TatA molecules represent only a small proportion of the total TatA present in the cell (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by the co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Constitutively associating TatA molecules are probably present at an equimolar ratio with TatC.
source: Indeed, earlier studies with overproduced Tat proteins suggest that such constitutively associating TatA molecules are probably present at a equimolar ratio with TatC (Bolhuis et al., 2001; Zoufaly et al., 2012) in contrast to the 50 to 100-fold molar excess of TatA over TatC found in cells (Berks et al., 2003; Jack et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The triple substitution variant MTQ abolished the interaction of TatB with TatC but had no effect on the co-immunoprecipitation of constitutively associated TatA with TatC.
source: The triple substitution variant MTQ was used to disrupt the polar cluster site on TatC. This change abolished the interaction of TatB with TatC but had no effect on the co-immunoprecipitation of constitutively associated TatA with TatC (Figure 6B, strain AE pBCFEA, MTQ, compare lanes 1 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The polar cluster site of TatC is occupied by TatB.
source: These observations suggest that the polar cluster site of TatC is occupied by TatB.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that disrupting the polar cluster abolishes TatB binding but not constitutive TatA binding.

claim: Constitutively associated TatA binds directly to TatC, rather than through TatB.
source: They also show that constitutively associated TatA binds directly to TatC, rather than through TatB, and that this interaction does not require the polar cluster.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that TatA still binds to TatC when TatB is removed from the polar cluster site.

claim: The E8A variant of TatB no longer co-immunoprecipitates with TatC.
source: If the polar cluster mediates TatB binding to TatC then the interaction between the two proteins should be abolished not only by eliminating the polar cluster site in TatC but also by removal of the TatB polar cluster residue E8. In agreement with this prediction, the E8A variant of TatB no longer co-immunoprecipitates with TatC (Figure 6B, compare lanes 9 and 10).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Introducing the Q8A substitution into TatA had no effect on substrate-independent binding of TatA to TatC.
source: By contrast, introducing the analogous Q8A substitution into TatA had no effect on substrate-independent binding of TatA to TatC (Figure 6B, compare lanes 9 and 11), consistent with the observed insensitivity of this interaction to removal of the TatC polar cluster (Figure 6B, lane 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: In the resting Tat system it is TatB that occupies the binding site located at TatC TM5/TM6.
source: Taken together, the effects of substituting potential polar cluster residues in all three Tat components indicate that the polar cluster is involved in connecting TatB to TatC. This suggests that in the resting Tat system it is TatB that occupies the binding site located at TatC TM5/TM6.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on polar cluster variants.

claim: MD simulations of the TatBC heterodimer model containing the polar cluster variants TatB E8A, TatC T208A, or TatC Q215A show that the periplasmic end of the TatB TMH is no longer tightly associated with TatC.
source: MD simulations of the TatBC heterodimer model containing the polar cluster variants TatB E8A, TatC T208A, or TatC Q215A show that the periplasmic end of the TatB TMH is no longer tightly associated with TatC (Figure 4A,B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1) in agreement with the experimental data that the polar cluster plays an important role in binding TatB to TatC.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: The TatC variants with single alanine substitutions within the polar cluster are unaffected in TatB binding.
source: Nevertheless, we observed that the TatC variants with single alanine substitutions within the polar cluster are unaffected in TatB binding (Figure 6B, compare lanes 1 and 3, 5 and 6, and 5 and 7)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Two of the single alanine substitution variants (T208A and Q215A) are severely compromised in Tat transport activity.
source: even though two of these variants are severely compromised in Tat transport activity (Figure 5A, strains AE pBCT208A and AE pBCQ215A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The polar cluster on TatC must have a mechanistic role in Tat transport beyond allowing complex formation with TatB.
source: Thus, these additional observations show that the polar cluster on TatC must have a mechanistic role in Tat transport beyond allowing complex formation with TatB.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that some variants retain TatB binding but lose transport activity.

claim: An arginine substitution of TatC polar cluster residue M205 was previously isolated in a screen for Tat transport-deficient mutants.
source: An arginine substitution of TatC polar cluster residue M205 was previously isolated in a screen for Tat transport-deficient mutants (Kneuper et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The M205R variant is unable to mediate Tat transport.
source: We confirmed the inability of this M205R variant to mediate Tat transport in the experimental system used in the current study (Figure 5; strain A pBCM205R).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Alanine substitution of M205 does not block Tat transport.
source: Since alanine substitution of the same residue does not block Tat transport (Figure 5A,B; strain AE pBCM205A) we deduce that it is the introduction of the arginine side chain, rather than loss of the methionine functionality, that prevents the M205R variant sustaining Tat transport.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: It is the introduction of the arginine side chain, rather than loss of the methionine functionality, that prevents the M205R variant sustaining Tat transport.
source: Since alanine substitution of the same residue does not block Tat transport (Figure 5A,B; strain AE pBCM205A) we deduce that it is the introduction of the arginine side chain, rather than loss of the methionine functionality, that prevents the M205R variant sustaining Tat transport.
evidence: This is an inference from comparing the effects of M205A and M205R substitutions.

claim: The TatC M205R substitution almost completely blocks complex formation with TatB.
source: Co-immunoprecipitation experiments show that the TatC M205R substitution almost completely blocks complex formation with TatB, in contrast to the M205A substitution which has no effect on the binding of TatB to TatC (Figure 6B; compare lanes 2 and 6).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The amount of TatA bound to TatC was markedly increased in the strain expressing the E8A variant of TatB.
source: Unexpectedly, the amount of TatA bound to TatC was markedly increased in the strain expressing the E8A variant of TatB (Figure 6B, compare lanes 9 and 10).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Removal of TatB from its binding site on TatC allows further TatA molecules to bind to TatC.
source: Since the E8A substitution compromises the ability of TatB to bind to TatC, one possible explanation for this phenomenon is that removal of TatB from its binding site on TatC allows further TatA molecules to bind to TatC (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that TatA binding increases when TatB binding is disrupted.

claim: TatA binding to TatC was also increased in a strain lacking TatB.
source: In agreement with this hypothesis we found that TatA binding to TatC was also increased in a strain lacking TatB (Figure 6B, compare lane 13 with lane 16).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The additional TatA molecules were binding to the site on TatC vacated by TatB.
source: We hypothesized that the additional TatA molecules were binding to the site on TatC vacated by TatB.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental observations.

claim: No enhancement of TatA binding was observed when the TatB binding site was disrupted through introducing either the MTQ or M205R substitutions into TatC.
source: Consistent with this idea, no enhancement of TatA binding was observed when the TatB binding site was disrupted through introducing either the MTQ or M205R substitutions into TatC (Figure 6B, compare lane 1 with lanes 2 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: A TatA Q8A substitution was able to block the increase in TatA binding to TatC seen when TatB is absent.
source: We found that a TatA Q8A substitution was able to block the increase in TatA binding to TatC seen when TatB is absent (Figure 6B, compare lane 15 with lanes 14 and 16) providing strong evidence that the enhanced TatA binding phenomenon corresponds to TatA molecules binding to the TM5/TM6 site on TatC.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: MD simulations of the TatAC dimer model containing a Q8A substitution support the view that this amino acid change would weaken the interaction of a TatA molecule bound at the TM5/TM6 site in TatC.
source: MD simulations of the TatAC dimer model containing a Q8A substitution support the view that this amino acid change would weaken the interaction of a TatA molecule bound at the TM5/TM6 site in TatC (Figure 4A,B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: Variants which prevent TatB associating with TatC (MTQ, M205R) were unable to form TatA-YFP oligomers.
source: Variants which prevent TatB associating with TatC (strains AyE pBCMTQ, AyE pBCM205R) were unable to form TatA-YFP oligomers, consistent with the previously reported phenotype of strains lacking the TatB protein (Leake et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Variants which retained TatBC interactions (T208A, Q215A) were still able to form protonophore-sensitive TatA-YFP oligomers.
source: whilst variants which retained TatBC interactions (strains AyE pBCT208A, AyE pBCQ215A) were still able to form protonophore-sensitive TatA-YFP oligomers.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The oligomerization behavior of the TatA Q8A variant was indistinguishable from that of the parental protein when all other Tat components were present.
source: We first examined cells in which all other Tat components were present, including the TatA paralogue TatE. In these cells the oligomerization behavior of the TatA Q8A variant was indistinguishable from that of the parental protein.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Q8 does not need to be present in a TatA protomer for that protein to be included within the TatA oligomer.
source: These observations demonstrate that Q8 does not need to be present in a TatA protomer for that protein to be included within the TatA oligomer.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the oligomerization behavior of the Q8A variant.

claim: The TatA Q8A variant is able to increase the Tat pathway activity of the TatE-containing strain.
source: Indeed, the TatA Q8A variant is able to increase the Tat pathway activity of the TatE-containing strain whether fused to YFP or not (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The variant TatA Q8A protein is incorporated into the Tat system in such a way that it can contribute to Tat function, albeit at a level considerably less than that supported by the wild-type TatA protein.
source: This shows that the variant TatA protein is incorporated into the Tat system in such a way that it can contribute to Tat function, albeit at a level considerably less than that supported by the wild-type TatA protein.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transport activity data.

claim: The wild-type TatA-YFP fusion exhibits perturbed behavior when TatE is absent, forming substrate and protonophore-insensitive oligomers.
source: We then examined the behavior of the TatAQ8A-YFP fusion when TatE is absent. Under these conditions the wild-type TatA-YFP fusion is known to exhibit perturbed behavior. TatA-YFP oligomers are present even without substrate overproduction and these oligomers are insensitive to protonophore treatment (Alcock et al., 2013; Leake et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The variant TatAQ8A-YFP fusion phenocopies the behavior of the parental fusion protein by forming substrate and protonophore-insensitive oligomers.
source: The variant TatAQ8A-YFP fusion again phenocopies the behavior of the parental fusion protein by forming substrate and protonophore-insensitive oligomers (Figure 7B, strains AyBC and AyQ8ABC).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Q8 is not essential for TatA to be assembled into an oligomer.
source: This provides further evidence that Q8 is not essential for TatA to be assembled into an oligomer and eliminates the possibility that the TatAQ8A-YFP-containing oligomers are held together by TatE.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the oligomerization behavior of the Q8A variant in the absence of TatE.

claim: A TatB E8A variant is reported to be fully active in previous studies.
source: For example, a TatB E8A variant is reported to be fully active (Barrett and Robinson, 2005; Hicks et al., 2003) while we find that this variant does not support Tat transport (Figure 5A,B, strain AE pBE8AC).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and comparison to the current study's data.

claim: The TatC M205R variant has previously been reported not to affect TatBC complex assembly.
source: Similarly, whilst we observe that the TatC M205R substitution almost completely blocks complex formation between TatB and TatC (Figure 6B), the same variant has previously been reported not to affect TatBC complex assembly (Kneuper et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work and comparison to the current study's data.

claim: Overproduction of the variant Tat systems resulted in the co-immunoprecipitation of TatB with TatC for the E8A and M205R variants.

claim: CueO export was substantially decreased in the TatB V18W variant.
source: CueO export was substantially decreased in the TatB V18W variant, and partially reduced in the TatC L21W variant, consistent with the perturbation of an important protein-protein interface (Figure 8A).

claim: All of the tryptophan substitutions induced partial dissociation of TatB from TatC when solubilized using the detergent lauryl maltose neopentyl glycol (LMNG).
source: Although the variant TatBC complexes remained intact following solubilization by digitonin, all of the tryptophan substitutions induced partial dissociation of TatB from TatC when solubilized using the detergent lauryl maltose neopentyl glycol (LMNG).

claim: The TatBC complex models show a hollow dome-shaped structure in which the concave surfaces of the TatC molecules face the interior of the particle.
source: The TatBC complex models show a hollow dome-shaped structure in which the concave surfaces of the TatC molecules face the interior of the particle (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is a description of the structural models built from co-evolution data.

claim: The modeled TatBC complexes were stable over the 100 ns simulation time in both lipid-filled and water-filled cavity scenarios.
source: The models were stable over the 100 ns simulation time in both scenarios suggesting significant structural cohesion within the protein complex and an ability to tolerate molecules of different polarities within the central cavity.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: The simulations with the water-filled cavity showed consistently higher mobility than the simulations with a lipid-filled cavity.
source: Nevertheless, the simulations with the water-filled cavity showed consistently higher mobility than the simulations with a lipid-filled cavity raising the possibility that over a longer time span only the lipid-supported cavity is stable.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: TatA and TatB compete for a single binding site on TatC.
source: In summary, we infer that TatA and TatB compete for a single binding site on TatC.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental and computational data.

claim: In the resting Tat system TatB has the higher affinity for the shared binding site on TatC.
source: In the resting Tat system TatB has the higher affinity for the site, while in the substrate-activated state TatA binding is favored.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental observations.

claim: In the substrate-activated state TatA binding is favored at the shared binding site on TatC.
source: In the resting Tat system TatB has the higher affinity for the site, while in the substrate-activated state TatA binding is favored.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental observations.

claim: The TatA molecule that is recruited to the shared binding site nucleates the uptake of further TatA molecules to form the transport-capable translocation complex.
source: We propose that the TatA molecule that is recruited to this shared binding site nucleates the uptake of further TatA molecules to form the transport-capable translocation complex (Figure 9).
evidence: This is a mechanistic model proposed based on the experimental and computational data.

claim: Conformational change at TM1 elicited by signal peptide binding can be envisaged to reposition the adjacent TatB TMH, thereby reducing its affinity for the TM5/TM6 site on the neighboring TatC molecule.
source: Thus, conformational change at TM1 elicited by signal peptide binding can be envisaged to reposition the adjacent TatB TMH, thereby reducing its affinity for the TM5/TM6 site on the neighboring TatC molecule.
evidence: This is a mechanistic speculation based on the structural model.

claim: Certain substitutions at or near the TatB TMH polar residue (E. coli TatB E8K or F9Q variants) permit the export of substrate proteins with defective signal peptides.
source: The proposal that substrate binding is mechanistically linked to displacement of TatB from the TM5/TM6 site is able to explain the otherwise puzzling earlier genetic observations that certain substitutions at or near the TatB TMH polar residue (E. coli TatB E8K or F9Q variants) permit the export of substrate proteins with defective signal peptides even though the substitutions do not fall within the signal peptide binding site of TatC (Kreutzenbeck et al., 2007; Lausberg et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The TatB E8K and F9Q substitutions work by reducing the activation barrier to TatB displacement so that even relatively weakly binding signal peptides are able to trigger the structural transformations leading to TatA uptake.
source: We, therefore, deduce that the TatB substitutions work by reducing the activation barrier to TatB displacement so that even relatively weakly binding signal peptides are able to trigger the structural transformations leading to TatA uptake.
evidence: This is an inference from the structural model and prior genetic data.
